findings.what: Some NDVI S3.13 numbers for pairs with BARDL (rival_bardl_h1) partly count variables BARDL does not use. A, B and the official outputs all share these numbers, and they change with the collation used to break ties. This is not a misreading: section 10 says BARDL's top-k sets follow name order.
findings.evidence:
At the variable level BARDL gives exactly 0 to 93 of the 96 variables in J, so its top-5, top-10 and top-20 sets are filled by name. All three sources use Python code-point order, which puts aet_total_mm first. That variable is not a BARDL input, but it is treeroute's number 4 (share 0.0468).

Effect on rival_bardl_h1|treeroute at the variable level (A = B = official):
- Jaccard top-5 = 0.25 counts aet_total_mm as shared. Without it the value is 1/9 = 0.111.
- Jaccard top-10 = 0.25. Without it the value is 3/17 = 0.176.
- Breaking ties by descending name gives top-5 = 0.111, and the chance overlap moves to wbal at top-10.

Across three collations (code-point ascending, case-insensitive, descending), other BARDL pair numbers move:
- variable level, bardl|treeroute: RBO p0.9 0.365 vs 0.325.
- variable level, bardl|rf: top-20-union Spearman 0.162 vs 0.038; RBO p0.95 0.241 vs 0.322.
- variable level, bardl|lgbm: top-20-union Spearman 0.111 vs 0.030.
- feature level, bardl|treeroute: Jaccard top-20 0.111 includes x__V02_total_precip_mm_roll3, a column BARDL does not read (0.143 case-insensitive); top-20-union Spearman -0.064 / -0.126 / 0.003.
- feature level, bardl|ridge: top-20-union Spearman -0.471 / -0.393 / -0.362.

No other pair, in any problem or at either level, has a top-k overlap that exists only through a tie, or any collation dependence above 1e-12 (script s41).

The main-text rows are unaffected:
- NDVI BARDL top-20-union Spearman: 0.38409 vs 0.38406.
- The median and its interval are identical under all three collations.
- RBO against the consensus changes only in the 8th decimal.
findings.fix: No number needs to change. In S3.13, label BARDL's Jaccard, RBO and top-20-union Spearman as driven by name-order ties among its non-inputs. For example, a footnote: aet_total_mm enters BARDL's top 5 only by name order, and without it rival_bardl_h1|treeroute Jaccard top-5 would be 0.11, not 0.25. Alternatively, the owner decides whether to show these BARDL cells at all.

findings.what: Not an error: PM2.5's main-text RBO against the consensus sits at the low edge of its own percentile interval, because its bootstrap distribution has two peaks. The cell will read 0.37 [0.36, 0.57], which is easy to misread.
findings.evidence:
- Value 0.3720, interval [0.3645, 0.5707]; A, B and official agree to the last digit.
- 91.1% of the 2,000 draws are above the full-sample value; the bootstrap median is 0.423.
- The histogram has two peaks.
- Cause: the consensus top 3 lie within 0.35 percentage points of each other (spi 0.0813, sst_anom_global_tropical 0.0791, hist_last 0.0778), and hist_last is treeroute's number 1. On draws where hist_last becomes the consensus number 1, the RBO jumps.
- For comparison, NDVI's RBO interval is centred: 41% of draws are above its value.
findings.fix: The number stays. Add a one-line note in the main table or in S3.13: the interval is asymmetric because the consensus's top variable changes across draws.

checked: METHOD: my own minimal code, written from PROTOCOL.md sections 5, 8 and 10 without reading compare_shap.py, shapv1_stats.py or A's or B's scripts. Scripts are in V\skeptic\numbers\scripts (s_lib.py, s00-s92); outputs are in V\skeptic\numbers\work. Readings: region = rows.parquet group; I = mean over regions of the within-region mean |phi|; a region drawn c times weighs c; S is weighted the same way; J = union over every model in per_lead's models of the players above 1e-12 of that model's total; ties are exact, broken by name in code-point ascending order; Spearman on average ranks, re-ranked within the top-20 union; RBO = (1-p) sum p^(d-1) X_d/d + p^n; TV = half the L1 distance; families from per-row sums of phiv; family shares over the 5 families; numpy percentiles; median of the rivals.

DRAWS: I regenerated all five matrices as SHA-256('shap_v1|AW4|

|0||')[:8] mod G (big-endian), and every entry equals the saved bootstrap_draws.npy. The SHA-256 of each file equals per_lead draws_sha256 (5/5). The integers index sorted(group), which equals first-appearance order (5/5). per_lead regions = G (37, 42, 40, 127, 133). Count per index ranges 1863-2156 against 2000 expected.

REGION LABELS: every sampled (unit, time) is in the lead-0 test export file of its group: 1000/1000 in each gridded problem; for coral, 1000/1000 by the export's group column (file names are URL-encoded). Every piece's (row, unit, group, time, year) equals the registered sample.parquet (29/29 pieces).

FILE INTEGRITY: for all 29 rows.parquet, the SHA-256 equals done.json sha256 and meta rows_sha256. The background_keys SHA-256 equals meta and done.json. The SHA-256 of sample.parquet is in SAMPLE_REGISTER.txt and equals per_lead sample_sha256 (5/5).

GLOBAL-INDEX RULE (my own read of the rivals' export lead_0\test; exact equality; a step where every unit is missing counts as one value): coral has nino34a; defo, fire and pm25 have 27; ndvi has 26. The result is the same with missing values ignored. No column fails only by a spread below 1e-4, and no variable has some but not all columns global. My passing column lists equal per_lead global_columns: coral 3, defo 81, fire 27, pm25 27, ndvi 151.

FAMILIES: my map (normal, then hist_*, then calendar/ctx:*, then the global rule, then local) equals per_lead families for every variable (coral 26, defo 121, fire 117, pm25 111, ndvi 117); 0 differences. With the 'first listed family wins' reading, calendar would become a global index; that would matter only for coral and the B1 runs, and it contradicts the family named 'context and calendar'.
VARIABLE MAPS: section 8's suffix-stripping rule reproduces every variable_map entry of all 29 meta.json files (0 differences).
ROW FILES: base + sum phi + resid = eta (max 8.8e-14), and sum phi = sum phiv (max 7.5e-15), in all 29 pieces. For ridge and BARDL, phiv = the sum of the member phi (max 3.6e-15).
KENDALL'S W tie correction: my W equals scipy friedmanchisquare Q/(m(n-1)) on coral, defo, pm25 and ndvi (difference at most 5e-16), and also the S/(m sum V) form.

B1 BACKGROUNDS: for fire, pm25 and ndvi, the B1 keys form one set per unit, a superset of every B2 set, with the same unit and all earlier than the explained row. Every B2 key has the same calendar month. Sizes: fire B2 2-16 / B1 126-191; pm25 17 / 199-204; ndvi 16-17 / 153-203. The defo B1 keys equal the main keys (16,000).

B1 RUN FACTS: defo log lines 24 and 30: 16,000 pairs, 465.9 s total, 464.3 s tree SHAP. Fire lines 20 and 26: 187,186 pairs, 2,636.6 s, 2,631.6 s. Both equal meta.json and done.json. Fire B1 meta: pass, all four checks true, background B1, 4,000 trees, no merges. players_nonzero 113 and variables_nonzero 96 equal my counts; no FAILED.json.

SENSITIVITY (not errors): weighting rows instead of regions would change NDVI W 0.6173 to 0.6170, median rho20 0.0699 to 0.0638 and RBO 0.4029 to 0.4041; PM2.5 median rho20 -0.0189 to -0.0274; coral W 0.7346 to 0.7441, RBO 0.6674 to 0.6509, and swap nino34a and hs in treeroute's top 3. J from the main-set models alone equals J in every problem. The tie collation changes no main-row number by more than 3e-5. RBO without the p^n tail would differ by 4e-5 (NDVI) and 8.5e-5 (PM2.5).
